blocks.text: Split the flow at authority boundaries. ProposalGateway returns generated wording only. EvidenceGateway loads last activity and open invoices, while EligibilityGateway checks current permission and record versions. ReviewStore owns removals and stage overrides. ApprovalCoordinator freezes reviewed inputs, and OutcomeReducer renders authoritative per-record results.

blocks.title: Authority changes only at typed boundaries
blocks.text: Generated content can explain a suggested lifecycle stage. Trusted product data determines eligibility, a person creates approval, and only an execution outcome confirms whether a customer record changed. Cancel and rollback remain separate commands with separate results.

The proposal recommends moving Acme from onboarding to active because its last activity was yesterday, moving Birch to collections because an invoice is forty-five days overdue, and moving Cedar to at-risk. The specialist removes Cedar and changes Acme's target before approving. During review, Birch is edited by another operator and Acme's permission is revoked.

blocks.text: Rejected alternative: an executable proposal object

A single object containing generated copy, evidence, permission flags, selection, and an apply method gives untrusted or stale data the shape of authority. Refreshing it can also overwrite local choices. Separate records add coordination work, yet identify who produced each fact and explain why an action became unavailable.

blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: AI produces generated proposal content. Product services add current evidence and eligibility. The specialist reviews and approves an exact version. Execution returns authoritative results for each customer record, which feed audit and recovery controls.
